mission_01: In this mission, you will learn to construct and validate Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), which are the foundational representation of causal relationships. A DAG encodes assumptions about which variables directly cause others, with nodes representing variables and directed edges representing causal effects. The acyclic property ensures no variable can cause itself through a chain of effects. You will use the networkx library to build a simple causal graph with three variables (X, Y, Z) where X influences both Y and Z, and Z also influences Y — forming a classic mediation structure. Understanding how to programmatically construct and inspect DAGs is essential before moving to more advanced causal inference techniques like do-calculus and causal identification.
